sentences.text: Zhanghenglong was an extinct herbivorous dinosaur belonging to the hadrosauroid iguanodont group.
The genus contains only one species, Zhanghenglong yangchengensis, known from a partial and disarticulated skull and postcranial skeleton.
Zhanghenglong differs significantly from other hadrosauroids by having two distinct autapomorphies: a strongly deflected posterior third of the maxilla and dentary teeth with specific ridge offsets.
Only one species of Zhanghenglong is known, represented by a partial, disarticulated skull and postcranial remains.
Remains of a euornithopod were uncovered at Zhoujiagou in Henan province in 2011.

The species Zhanghenglong yangchengensis was named and described in 2014 by a team including Xing Hai, Wang Deyou, Han Fenglu, Corwin Sullivan, Ma Qingyu, He Yiming, David Hone, Yan Ronghao, Du Fuming, and Xu Xing.
Zhanghenglong lived during the Late Cretaceous, specifically the middle Santonian stage.
Fossils of Zhanghenglong were found in the Majiacun Formation in Xixia County, Henan Province, China.
Zhanghenglong lived between 85.7 and 83.6 million years ago during the Santonian stage.
